comment-nav-discoverability design (.design/comment-nav-discoverability.md): File switching in the Comments view is bound only to `[` / `]` and hinted only in a pane title, so it is undiscoverable — a user could not find how to change files. Add `←` / `→` as file-switch keys (spatially natural beside the left files rail) and a per-view key legend in the header, so the navigation is visible without reading source. adversarial review of comment-nav-discoverability: SHIP. Independent Opus review. The or-pattern guard KeyCode::Char('[') | KeyCode::Left if view==Comments applies to both alternatives (Rust semantics), Left/Right are bound nowhere else (j/k arms use Up/Down), so outside Comments they fall through to _ => {} — no panic, no shadowing. view_header legend is gated to Comments (_ => "") and non-Comments spacing is byte-identical, so no header assertion breaks; view_header(Browser) still carries its tabs. Title hints (←/→) embed via plain format!, no width/index panic, multibyte arrows fine. Two new tests genuine (header legend present + Browser lacks the comment hint; select_comment_file ±1/clamp). 77 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean; no stale assertion of the old '[ ] switch file' title. Verdict: SHIP.
